overviewFacts: Deal teams who live in email

overview.label: Overview
overview.heading: Capture deal context where it arrives
paras: For investment teams, most deal information arrives by email: a banker's teaser, a founder's update, a model in an attachment. The Kelp plugin opens as a panel beside the email and lets the user save it to Kelp in one pass: pick the people involved, link the deals or companies it belongs to, choose what to save, and add it.
We designed the panel to fit the inbox rather than compete with it: narrow, scannable and fast enough that saving to Kelp becomes a habit instead of a chore at the end of the week.

problemStatement: How might we make saving an email to the right deal so quick, from inside the inbox, that the deal record stays complete without anyone chasing it?

empathy.heading: Who we designed for
empathy.intro: Deal teams spend much of the day in email. Anything that asks them to leave it, open another tool and re-enter information tends not to happen.

people.context: Receive most of the deal flow and diligence material, and are expected to keep records up to date.
Hold relationships and conversations that the rest of the team needs to see, without being asked for them.
Wants relationship and deal history captured centrally, not trapped in individual inboxes.

painPoints: Important context lived in individual inboxes and never reached the shared record.
Saving an email to the right deal meant switching tools and copying details by hand.
One email often concerned several people and several deals or companies at once.
Attachments such as models and reports had to be downloaded and uploaded again.

challenges.label: The challenge
challenges.heading: A second product inside someone else's

items.title: Limited space
items.body: The panel shares the screen with the inbox, so every control has to earn its place in a narrow column.

items.title: Many-to-many links
items.body: One email can involve several contacts and belong to a deal, a portfolio company and a company at the same time.

items.title: Speed over completeness
items.body: If saving takes more than a few seconds, people stop doing it. The flow had to be fast with good defaults.

steps.title: Follow the email
steps.body: We traced what happens to a deal email today: who receives it, what they do with it and where the information should end up. That defined the three decisions the panel needs: who, which deal or company, and what to save.

steps.title: One panel, three steps
steps.body: We structured the panel top to bottom: choose profiles from the people on the email, choose projects (deals, portfolio companies or companies), then choose actions such as saving the email as an interaction and keeping its attachments.

steps.title: Fast multi-select
steps.body: Project search shows each result's type, deal, portfolio or company, and selected items become removable chips, so linking an email to several records is quick and reversible.

steps.title: Fit the host and the system
steps.body: We kept the panel visually quiet next to the inbox and built it from the same components as the rest of Kelp, so it feels like part of the product, not an add-on.

solution.label: The experience we created
solution.heading: Save to Kelp in one pass
paras: A side panel that turns 'I should log this' into a few clicks: the people on the email are suggested, deals and companies are a search away, attachments come along, and Add to Kelp files it all to the right records.

items.title: In-inbox panel
items.body: Opens beside the email, so users never leave their inbox to update Kelp.

items.title: Choose profiles
items.body: People on the email are listed for quick selection, so the right contacts are linked.

items.title: Choose projects
items.body: Search across deals, portfolio companies and companies, each labelled by type, and select several at once.

items.title: Save as an interaction
items.body: Log the email as an interaction on the selected records, so relationship history builds itself.

items.title: Keep attachments
items.body: Save the email's attachments to Kelp along with the message.

items.title: One clear action
items.body: A single Add to Kelp button at the end of the panel commits the whole selection.

faq.a: A plugin that works inside the inbox: tag an email's contacts, link it to the right deals, portfolio companies or companies, and save it with its attachments to Kelp in a few clicks.

faq.q: What problem did the Kelp plugin solve?
faq.a: The panel shares the screen with the inbox, so every control has to earn its place in a narrow column. The question we set out to answer: How might we make saving an email to the right deal so quick, from inside the inbox, that the deal record stays complete without anyone chasing it?

faq.q: How did Designit approach the Kelp plugin?
faq.a: We worked in 4 phases: Follow the email; one panel, three steps; fast multi-select; fit the host and the system. We traced what happens to a deal email today: who receives it, what they do with it and where the information should end up.

faq.q: Why do investment teams need an email plugin for their CRM?
faq.a: Because most deal information arrives by email. If logging it means leaving the inbox, it gets skipped and the shared record goes stale. A plugin that saves the email, its contacts and attachments to the right deal from the inbox keeps the record complete.

faq.q: How do you design a plugin panel that people actually use?
faq.a: Make it narrow, fast and predictable: the same three steps every time, good defaults from the email itself, and one clear final action. Anything that slows down a busy inbox will be ignored.

faq.q: How do you link one email to several deals or companies?
faq.a: With searchable multi-select. In the Kelp plugin each search result shows whether it is a deal, a portfolio company or a company, and every selection becomes a chip that can be removed before saving.

faq.q: What is relationship intelligence in private markets?
faq.a: Capturing who the firm knows and how it has interacted with them, from emails and meetings, so the whole team can see relationships and history. Saving emails as interactions on the right records is how the plugin feeds that picture.
